previous_disclosures.summary: Citigroup's 2023 operating expenses totaled $56.4 billion, a 10% increase from the prior year, which included $1.7 billion in FDIC special assessment charges, $780 million in restructuring charges, and $372 million in divestiture-related impacts. Excluding divestiture-related impacts, expenses were $56 billion, and excluding those plus the restructuring and FDIC charges, expenses of $53.5 billion increased 6%, driven by increased investments in risk, controls, technology, severance, and transformation.

current_disclosures.summary: Citigroup's operating expenses decreased 4% to $54.0 billion in 2024, with a 2% decrease to $53.8 billion excluding FDIC special assessments. The decline was driven by organizational simplification savings, reduced restructuring charges, and repositioning costs, partially offset by higher volume-related expenses and costs associated with a July 2024 Civil Money Penalty Consent Order.

comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense decreased $2.4 billion to $1.7 billion, primarily due to the absence of a $2.1 billion prior-year accrual for the FDIC special assessment following the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, along with lower expenses from liquidating business activities.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Bank of America identify the FDIC special assessment as a key driver of noninterest expense variance between 2023 and 2024, but the nature of the impact differs. Citigroup reports that excluding FDIC special assessments (and divestitures) expenses decreased 2%, implying the assessment was a headwind or normalization factor against which underlying efficiency was measured. In contrast, Bank of America highlights that its 2024 expense decrease of $2.4 billion was primarily due to the 'absence of a $2.1 billion prior-year accrual' for the FDIC special assessment recorded in 2023. While C's metric isolates the 2024 assessment impact alongside divestitures, BAC's variance is structurally driven by the one-time 2023 charge no longer being present in 2024.

sentences.text: Excluding the FDIC special assessment and divestiture-related impacts, expenses of $53.5 billion also decreased 2%.

Noninterest expense decreased $2.4 billion to $1.7 billion primarily due to the $2.1 billion accrual recorded in the prior year for the FDIC special assessment resulting from the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, and lower expenses related to a liquidating business activity.

comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses decreased 2% to $33.77 billion in 2024, aided by lower CIE commercial real estate impairments and prior year one-time charges like the GreenSky write-down, partially offset by higher compensation and transaction expenses, resulting in an efficiency ratio improvement to 63.1% from 74.6%.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs report a 2% decrease in operating expenses for 2024 compared to 2023, with FDIC-related charges serving as a significant differentiator in the year-over-year variance. Citigroup's 2% decline excludes both FDIC special assessments and divestiture-related impacts. Goldman Sachs also reports a 2% decrease to $33.77 billion, driven by significant prior-year charges (impairments, GreenSky write-down) and a $529 million FDIC special assessment fee recognized in 2023. However, GS recognized an *additional* $71 million in FDIC fees in 2024, whereas C excludes its 2024 assessment impact entirely from the adjusted metric. Both firms demonstrate efficiency gains, but GS's decrease is heavily influenced by the non-repetition of massive 2023 impairments, while C's narrative focuses on operational efficiency excluding regulatory shocks.

sentences.text: Excluding the FDIC special assessment and divestiture-related impacts, expenses of $53.5 billion also decreased 2%.

Operating expenses were $33.77 billion for 2024, 2% lower than 2023, reflecting decreases driven by significantly lower expenses, including impairments, related to commercial real estate in consolidated investment entities (CIEs) and other significant expenses recognized in the prior year, including the write-down of identifiable intangible assets related to GreenSky Holdings, LLC (GreenSky), an impairment of goodwill related to Consumer platforms and the FDIC special assessment fee.

comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense was $91.8 billion, up 5%, driven by higher compensation and a $1.0 billion Visa share contribution to the foundation, partially offset by lower FDIC-related expenses due to the timing of special assessments.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase analyze the impact of FDIC special assessments on their 2024 operating expenses relative to 2023, but they report opposite headline trends due to differing base-year pressures. JPMorgan reports a 5% increase in noninterest expense ($91.8 billion), explicitly noting that this increase was 'partially offset by lower FDIC-related expense' because 2023 included a large $2.9 billion special assessment. Conversely, Citigroup reports a 2% decrease in expenses ($53.5 billion) excluding FDIC impacts, suggesting that after removing the 2024 assessment cost, underlying expenses were lower. Both disclosures confirm that the 2023 period was characterized by a significant one-time FDIC charge ($2.9B for JPM, $1.7B+ for C implied by context) that suppressed 2024 comparisons or required exclusion for meaningful analysis.

sentences.text: Excluding the FDIC special assessment and divestiture-related impacts, expenses of $53.5 billion also decreased 2%.

• Noninterest expense was $91.8 billion, up 5%, driven by higher compensation expense, including higher revenue-related compensation and growth in the number of employees, as well as a $1.0 billion contribution of Visa shares to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation recorded in the second quarter of 2024, partially offset by lower FDIC-related expense, reflecting a $2.9 billion special assessment recognized in the fourth quarter of 2023, compared with a $725 million increase to the FDIC special assessment recognized in the first quarter of 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: Non-interest expenses totaled $19,129 million in 2024, a 5% increase year-over-year, driven by higher compensation and benefits (primarily discretionary incentive compensation) and higher non-compensation expenses (primarily execution-related and technology spend).
comparisons.comparison: While Citigroup isolates FDIC special assessments to show a 2% expense decrease, Morgan Stanley reports a 5% increase in total non-interest expenses. MS notes that 'Non-compensation expenses' decreased, driven by 'lower FDIC special assessment cost,' similar to the benefit C sees by excluding it. However, MS's overall expense growth was driven by higher compensation and benefits. Unlike C, which presents an adjusted metric that removes the assessment to highlight operational efficiency, MS includes the assessment in the total but identifies it as a favorable variance component within non-compensation expenses. Both firms acknowledge the FDIC assessment as a specific line item impacting expenses, but C's disclosure strategy uses exclusion to frame a 2% reduction, whereas MS uses inclusion to frame a 5% increase despite the FDIC benefit.

sentences.text: Excluding the FDIC special assessment and divestiture-related impacts, expenses of $53.5 billion also decreased 2%.
